fact_text: An employer-specific work permit is tied to the specific employer, location and occupation named on it; the permit's Additional Information section lists the employer, location and occupation you are authorized for, and you must comply with everything listed on it.
evidence_quote: Additional Information – includes the employer, location and occupation

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work permit lets you work anywhere for anyone. Actually most employer-sponsored permits are employer-specific: they name the employer, location and occupation, and you cannot change employer, job or location without new authorization from IRCC. Action: confirm the permit conditions before starting, and apply to change conditions before switching employers.

entity_title: You cannot work before your work permit is issued
fact_text: A foreign national who needs a work permit and does not yet have one cannot legally work in Canada; you generally cannot begin working before your work permit is issued.
evidence_quote: If you need a work permit and don’t yet have one, you can’t

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can start work once you have a job offer or have applied. Actually you cannot legally work until the permit is issued. Action: do not agree a start date before the permit (or, for outside-Canada applicants, the approval to start) is in hand.

fact_text: For an employer-specific work permit your Canadian employer usually needs a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) — a document proving there is a need to hire a foreign worker — before you can apply. Most jobs need an LMIA.
evidence_quote: A labour market impact assessment (LMIA) is a document that proves there’s a need to hire a foreign worker to fill the job. Most jobs need an LMIA.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the worker gets the LMIA. Actually the employer obtains the LMIA (and gives you the LMIA letter and Annex A) before you can apply for the work permit. Action: your permit application depends on the employer completing the LMIA first, which adds lead time.

fact_text: Some work permits are LMIA-exempt: under the International Mobility Program (IMP) an employer can hire a temporary foreign worker without a Labour Market Impact Assessment. If an LMIA is required the job cannot go through the IMP and must instead go through the Temporary Foreign Worker Program.
evidence_quote: Under the International Mobility Program (IMP), you can hire a temporary foreign worker without a labour market impact assessment (LMIA).

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed every foreign worker needs an LMIA. Actually LMIA-exempt work permits exist under the International Mobility Program (categories such as intra-company transferees and free-trade / CUSMA professionals). Action: check whether the role is LMIA-exempt, which removes the LMIA step and is usually much faster.

fact_text: The Global Talent Stream is an LMIA-required stream of the Temporary Foreign Worker Program for highly skilled workers; it is not an LMIA exemption. Eligible applications can qualify for two-week Global Skills Strategy processing.
evidence_quote: LMIA-required highly skilled workers hired under the Global Talent Stream

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly grouped with LMIA-exempt routes. Actually the Global Talent Stream requires an LMIA — it is part of the Temporary Foreign Worker Program and offers fast (2-week) Global Skills Strategy processing rather than an LMIA exemption. Action: expect an LMIA step for GTS, but a fast one.

entity_title: Express Entry is a permanent-residence route
fact_text: Express Entry is the online system for managing permanent-residence (immigration) applications from skilled workers — it is a separate route from a temporary work permit that an employer-sponsored professional uses to come and work in Canada.
evidence_quote: Express Entry is an online system that we use to manage immigration applications from skilled workers.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly confused with a work permit. Actually Express Entry is a permanent-residence application (its own eligibility, fees and processing), distinct from the temporary work permit you use to start working. Action: treat PR via Express Entry as a separate, later application from the work permit that gets you into the job.

entity_title: Social Insurance Number (SIN) required to work
fact_text: To work in Canada you need a Social Insurance Number (SIN), a 9-digit identifier issued by Service Canada; you also need it to access government programs and benefits.
evidence_quote: To work in Canada or access government programs and benefits, you need a 9-digit identifier known as Social Insurance Number (SIN).

entity_title: A temporary resident's SIN expires with their immigration documents
fact_text: A temporary resident's SIN expires with their immigration documents, so you must extend your SIN when you extend or change your work permit.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a SIN is permanent. Actually a temporary resident's SIN (beginning with 9) expires with the work permit. Action: after each permit extension, update/extend your SIN with Service Canada or an employer may be unable to keep paying you.

entity_title: Residents are taxed on worldwide income
fact_text: An individual who is resident in Canada for a tax year is subject to Canadian income tax on their worldwide income from all sources (a non-resident is generally taxed only on income from Canadian sources).
evidence_quote: An individual who is resident in Canada during a tax year is subject to Canadian income tax on his or her worldwide income from all sources.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you are taxed only on Canadian earnings. Actually once you are a Canadian tax resident you are taxed on worldwide income from all sources. Action: plan for foreign income, and check any tax treaty between Canada and your home country.

entity_title: Tax residency begins with residential ties, often from day one
fact_text: You become a resident of Canada for income tax purposes when you have enough residential ties in Canada; for most newcomers this starts the first day you live in Canada.
evidence_quote: You become a resident of Canada for income tax purposes when you have enough residential ties in Canada. For most newcomers, this starts the first day you live in Canada.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed tax residency starts only after some months or once you get PR. Actually it is based on residential ties (a home, spouse/partner, dependants) and for most newcomers starts the first day you live in Canada. Action: your Canadian tax clock can start on arrival — a case-specific determination that a treaty tie-breaker can change.

entity_title: Immigration status does not determine tax obligations
fact_text: Your immigration status tells you whether you can live, work or study in Canada, but — unlike your tax residency status — it does not determine your tax obligations.
evidence_quote: Unlike your residency status, it does not tell you your tax obligations.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed being on a temporary work permit means you are not a Canadian taxpayer. Actually tax residency is separate from immigration status; a temporary resident can be a Canadian tax resident. Action: assess tax residency on residential ties, not on the type of permit you hold.

entity_title: First tax return timing for newcomers
fact_text: As a newcomer you are not required to file a Canadian tax return until the year after you become a resident for tax purposes; the return is generally due by April 30 of the following year.
evidence_quote: As a newcomer to Canada, you are not required to do your taxes until the year after you become a resident for tax purposes.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you must file immediately on arrival. Actually your first return is due the year after you become a tax resident (usually by April 30). Action: keep records of foreign income from before arrival, as it can be needed to calculate benefits and credits.

fact_text: Ontario health insurance (OHIP) no longer has a waiting period: if you are eligible, coverage is immediate.
evidence_quote: There is no longer a waiting period for OHIP coverage. If you are eligible, you will have immediate health insurance coverage.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed there is a 3-month OHIP waiting period. Actually the waiting period was removed (in 2020); coverage is immediate once you are eligible. Action: apply as soon as you arrive rather than waiting three months.

fact_text: A work-permit holder can qualify for OHIP if they are in Ontario on a valid work permit and are working full-time in Ontario, for an Ontario employer, for at least 6 months (their spouse and dependants may then also qualify); applicants must also meet the physical-presence and primary-residence minimums and apply in person at a ServiceOntario centre.
evidence_quote: are in Ontario on a valid work permit and are working full-time in Ontario, for an Ontario employer, for at least 6 months

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any work-permit holder gets OHIP on arrival. Actually eligibility requires a valid work permit plus full-time work in Ontario for an Ontario employer for at least 6 months. Action: bridge the gap with private/employer health insurance until you qualify.

entity_title: 60 days to switch to an Ontario licence
fact_text: When you move to Ontario you can drive on a valid licence from another province, state or country for 60 days; after 60 days you must switch to an Ontario driver's licence.
evidence_quote: When you move to Ontario, you can use a valid licence from another province, state or country for 60 days. After 60 days, you need to switch to an Ontario driver’s licence.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a foreign licence is valid for a year or for your whole stay. Actually you have only 60 days after moving before you must switch. Action: start the Ontario licence process early.

entity_title: Licence exchange only from jurisdictions with an agreement
fact_text: Ontario exchanges a foreign licence for a full Ontario licence only for listed jurisdictions with an exchange agreement; a driver from a jurisdiction without an agreement must pass the vision, knowledge and G2 road tests, wait at least 12 months, and then pass the G road test.
evidence_quote: wait at least 12 months before attempting the G road test

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any foreign licence can be swapped directly. Actually only listed jurisdictions can exchange; drivers from other countries effectively re-enter graduated licensing — tests plus a 12-month wait before the full G test. Action: check whether your country has an exchange agreement before you rely on a quick swap.
